title: Gerund vs infinitive
titleVi: Danh động từ và động từ nguyên mẫu
summary: Hai danh sách động từ, ba cặp đổi nghĩa, và cách dùng danh động từ làm chủ ngữ trong văn học thuật.
whyItMatters: Đây là lỗi ngữ pháp phổ biến nhất của người Việt ở band 6.5–7.0: *I enjoy to read*, *She suggested to go*. Mỗi động từ tiếng Anh quyết định dạng theo sau nó, và tiếng Việt không có cơ chế này — *thích đọc* dùng cùng một động từ cho mọi trường hợp. Sai dạng động từ xuất hiện ở hầu như mọi câu, nên nó ảnh hưởng tới điểm Grammatical Range nhiều hơn bất kỳ lỗi đơn lẻ nào khác.

sections.heading: Verb + -ing: a closed list worth memorising
body: Some verbs are followed only by the **-ing** form. The list is finite, so it can be learned: *enjoy, mind, suggest, recommend, admit, avoid, imagine, finish, consider, deny, risk, fancy, keep, mention, involve*.
Phrasal verbs take -ing as well: *give up*, *put off*, *go on / carry on*, *keep on*, *end up*, *look into*. *He gave up smoking* — never *gave up to smoke*.

The -ing form here is a **gerund**: it behaves like a noun, so it can be the subject, the object of a preposition, or the object of the verb. That noun quality is why it appears after prepositions: *I'm tired of waiting*, *She's good at solving problems*.

rows: We should avoid making vague claims.
They are considering raising the fees.
Do you mind waiting a few minutes?
Postponing now risks losing the funding.
She kept asking the same question.
They put off announcing the results.

sections.heading: Verb + to-infinitive: the other list
body: Other verbs take only the **to-infinitive**: *offer, plan, manage, deserve, agree, arrange, fail, afford, refuse, hope, promise, learn, decide, forget, threaten, tend, seem, appear, pretend, claim*.

Many of these express intention, effort or outcome — which is why the infinitive (the "to do" form) fits: *They decided to relocate*, *The plan failed to reduce traffic*, *She managed to finish on time*.
After **seem, appear, pretend, claim** you can use *to be doing* or *to have done* to place the action in time: *The policy seems to be working*, *He claims to have visited forty countries*.

rows: They arranged to meet the following week.
The campaign failed to change behaviour.
The council refused to publish the figures.
Few families can afford to buy in the centre.
The gap appears to be widening.
The company claims to have cut emissions by half.
He promised not to mention the incident.

sections.heading: Same verb, different meaning
body: A small group accepts both forms with a **change of meaning**. These are the highest-value items on the list because they are tested directly and they are easy to get wrong in writing.

**remember/forget doing** = you did it and now recall (or fail to recall) it. **remember/forget to do** = a duty you did or did not carry out. **regret doing** = you are sorry about something in the past. **regret to say/tell/inform** = you are about to give bad news, a formal formula. **go on doing** = continue the same activity; **go on to do** = move to the next item.
**stop doing** = end the activity. **stop to do** = pause in order to do something else. **try to do** = attempt something difficult. **try doing** = experiment with a solution.

rows: I recalled doing it — the memory came back.
I remembered to lock the door.
I did not forget the duty.
She paused her journey in order to smoke.
He went on talking for an hour.
He went on to talk about costs.
He moved to the next topic.
I am sorry about the past decision.
We regret to inform you that...
Attempt it, though it may be difficult.

sections.heading: Verb + somebody + -ing
body: Some -ing verbs take a person in the middle: **stop somebody doing**, **keep somebody doing**, **imagine somebody doing**, **remember somebody doing**, **prevent somebody from doing**.
Note the difference between *stop somebody doing* (no preposition) and *prevent somebody from doing* (with *from*). Both are correct; mixing them — *stop people from to do* — is not.
The possessive is possible and slightly more formal: *I remember his saying that...* Most IELTS candidates can safely use the object form: *I remember him saying that...*

examples.right: The new rules stop companies dumping waste in the river.
examples.wrong: The new rules stop companies to dump waste in the river.

examples.right: Nothing will prevent them from expanding the airport.
I can't imagine living without a car.
examples.note: No person needed when the meaning is general.

sections.heading: Gerunds as subjects: the academic workhorse
body: A gerund can be the subject of a sentence, which makes it one of the most useful tools in Task 2: *Investing in public transport reduces congestion.* *Charging drivers to enter the city centre has proved controversial.*

This pattern replaces the clumsy infinitive subject. *To invest in public transport reduces congestion* is grammatical but heavy; English prefers the gerund, or an abstract noun (*Investment in public transport...*).

Gerunds also compress two clauses into one, which raises your score for grammatical range while shortening the sentence: *Many students work part-time, which leaves them little time for study* becomes *Working part-time leaves many students little time for study.*

examples.right: Raising the retirement age would ease pressure on the pension system.
examples.note: Gerund subject plus conditional — compact and formal.

examples.right: There is little point in banning cars without improving buses.
examples.note: **there is little point in + -ing** is a band-7.5 evaluation frame.

examples.right: Banning cars from the centre is easier said than done.
examples.wrong: To ban cars from the centre is easier said than done.
examples.note: Both are grammatical, but the gerund is the natural choice.

commonMistakes.wrong: I enjoy to read about history.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt *thích đọc* không phân biệt dạng động từ, nên người học dịch thẳng sang *enjoy to read*. **enjoy** chỉ đi với **-ing**.

commonMistakes.wrong: She suggested to postpone the meeting.
commonMistakes.why: **suggest** không nhận to-infinitive. Dùng *suggest + -ing* hoặc *suggest that + mệnh đề*: *She suggested that we postpone the meeting.*

commonMistakes.wrong: Remember locking the door before you leave.
commonMistakes.right: Remember to lock the door before you leave.
commonMistakes.why: *Remember doing* nghĩa là **nhớ lại việc đã làm**; *remember to do* mới là **nhớ phải làm**. Câu này nói về bổn phận sắp tới nên phải dùng to-infinitive — lỗi này làm đổi hẳn nghĩa câu.

commonMistakes.wrong: He stopped to smoke last year and feels much healthier.
commonMistakes.right: He stopped smoking last year and feels much healthier.
commonMistakes.why: *Stop to smoke* nghĩa là **dừng lại để hút thuốc**, ngược hoàn toàn với ý *cai thuốc*. Với nghĩa từ bỏ thói quen phải dùng **stop + -ing**.

commonMistakes.right: My phone needs repairing. / My phone needs to be repaired.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt *cần được sửa* khiến người học giữ dạng bị động *repaired*. Sau **need** phải là **-ing** (mang nghĩa bị động) hoặc **to be + V3**.

ieltsTips: Dùng danh động từ làm chủ ngữ để câu gọn và học thuật: `Investing in rural clinics would reduce infant mortality.`
Học động từ theo cụm, không học riêng lẻ: ghi `succeed in -ing`, `lead to -ing`, `be worth -ing` như một khối.
Trong Task 2, `there is little point in + -ing` và `it is worth + -ing` là hai khung đánh giá rất tự nhiên ở band 7.5+.
Khi không chắc một động từ đi với dạng nào, thay bằng cụm an toàn: `make it possible to...`, `lead to + noun`. Đừng đoán.

exercises.question: The council is considering ___ the bus fare for students.
She managed ___ the report before the deadline.
I clearly remember ___ the letter, so it must be somewhere.
exercises.explanation: *Remember doing* = nhớ lại việc đã làm; câu này khẳng định ký ức nên dùng **posting**.

exercises.question: The government failed ___ the promised reforms.
Which sentence is correct?
options: They suggested us to take the train.
They suggested to take the train.
exercises.explanation: **suggest + -ing** (hoặc *suggest that we take*). Không dùng *suggest + tân ngữ + to V*.

exercises.question: We should avoid ___ (use) informal language in Task 2.
He admitted ___ (make) a serious error in the calculation.
exercises.explanation: **admit + -ing**; dạng *having made* cũng đúng nhưng ít dùng hơn.

exercises.question: They decided ___ (postpone) the launch until the spring.
Please remember ___ (turn off) the lights when you leave.
exercises.explanation: Bổn phận cần nhớ để làm → **remember to do**.

exercises.question: The old bridge needs ___ (repair) before winter.
exercises.explanation: **need + -ing** mang nghĩa bị động, hoặc **need to be + V3**.
